notes: Runs: all five have rc 0, head d04061d with uncommitted false, reads empty and skills_listed 209. None of the sessions ran mix format or invoked a skill; the transcripts mention SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md nowhere except in the Skill tool's definition.

Rules: git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes only SKILL.md's Read required keys rule (two new paragraphs), In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use (rewritten), and ex_unit.md's capture_log rule (one added sentence). None of these is in macro-dsl's index list, and macros.md and library-design.md are untouched, so all eight rules graded here are unchanged and are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/macro-dsl-baseline.json and macro-dsl-skill.json. The per-bullet counts asked for the rewritten rules apply to webhook-parser and library-client, whose case files carry those bullets; macro-dsl's What to check list has no such bullets and none of its runs is graded against the rewritten rules, so no per-sentence count is recorded here.

Standard carried over: a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, while validation in the macro body outside quote does not; the use documentation rule needs the effects of use in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and prose or nothing is violated; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden in all five runs); `unless` is listed under the branching rule, `if`/`cond` validation is not; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a catch-all public match clause is listed under Make polymorphism explicit; a keyword list passed inline over several lines to raise is listed under Build a multi-line argument; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens, and any other reflow is listed under Before you finish.

Do: rule, deciding sentence "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper.": 2 of 5. haiku-1 lines 101-102 (130 characters joined) and 104-105 (99 joined) and sonnet-1 lines 56-57 (99 joined, inside the quote); the sessions wrote them wrapped, and mix format on the joined lines wraps them again (checked). sonnet-1 lines 98-100 are a head broken after a long guard (111 joined), the one wrap the rule keeps. Opus clean, Haiku violated, Sonnet violated (2026-10-22-d baseline: Opus clean, Haiku clean, Sonnet violated).

Compile-time dependencies were checked with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects, one per run, with the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex and real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app/handlers.ex. opus-1 reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (runtime) at lines 132-133: it calls Macro.expand(handler, %{env | function: {:match, 1}}) (line 118), which the rule's "expand it as if it were used inside that function" describes, so it is clean although the case text says Macro.expand/2 makes it compile-time (that holds only without a function in the env). The other four call Macro.expand(handler, caller) with the caller's env unchanged and report both handlers as (compile).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project was loaded, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail while get expands: ArgumentError in opus-1 and sonnet-1, CompileError in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2. All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Format: mix format adds parentheses to the two get calls in all five runs (result.json format_ok is false for that reason); it also reflows opus-1 lines 100 and 103 and haiku-1 lines 72 and 84, listed under Before you finish.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order and match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", returning :error for "/nope". haiku-1 returns atom param keys (%{id: "42"}, via String.to_atom on the route string, line 92), as its @moduledoc says; the others use string keys. match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 and returns :error in sonnet-1 (catch-all clause). String.to_atom on route strings (haiku-1 line 92, sonnet-1 line 119) is source code, not external input, so it is not counted under the atom rule.

Against 2026-10-22-d baseline: opus-1 moves from violated to clean on the compile-time-dependency rule (Macro.expand with a function env). sonnet-2 now specs routes/0 and match/1 and has no public helper, so it is clean on the spec rule; sonnet-1 now has no @doc false helper but leaves routes/0 and match/1 unspecced, so the Sonnet tier stays violated. haiku-1 wrote bind/3 as wrapped do: clauses, so the Haiku tier moves from clean to violated on the do: rule. Every run again records the route by a direct attribute write inside get's quote and has no admonition; Write a function unless the job needs a macro, Unquote each argument once and Write module names literally stay clean in all five.
